BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://vmw.dilg.gov-ph DU-G OPINION NO. 59 22 BRYAN G. PIADOCHE Purok 1, Pisaan, San Francisco, Agusan del Sur Dear Mr. Piadoche: This has reference to your letter dated I March 2024 seeking legal opinion from this Department on the following: 1. Is the maximum penalty for barangay ordinances under RA 7160 indeed capped at Php 1,000? 2. If so, does the Barangay Local Government Unit (BLGU)'s decision to impose a higher fine constitute a violation of this provision of RA 7160? Per your representation, the Punong Barangay of Barangay Prosperidad is imposing a fine of Php 5,000.00 for littering offenders. You mentioned that the PB further explained that the decision to adopt the provincial ordinance, prescribing a penalty of PHP 5,000.00, was due to its perceived greater deterrent effect With this, you represented that the ordinance is in contradiction with Section 516 of the Local Government Code. Thus, the request for legal opinion. At the onset, we invite your attention to Section 516 of the LGC which specifically states: "Section 516. Penalties for Violation of Tax Ordinances. - The sanggunian of a local government unit is authorized to prescribe fines or other penalties for violation of tax ordinances but in no case shall such fines be less than One thousand pesos (Pl ,OOO.OO) nor more than Five thousand pesos (P5,000.OO), nor shall imprisonment be less than one (1) month nor more than six (6) months. Such fine or other penalty, or both, shall be imposed at the discretion of the court. The sangguniang barangay may prescribe a fine of not less than One hundred pesos (PIOO.OO) nor more than One thousand pesos (PI ,OOO.OO)." The preceding paragraph explicitly addresses the penalty for violating tax ordinances, rather than general ordinance violations. As a result, you cited this provision incorrectly because it is not applicable in the matter at hand. Be that as it may, as to the first query, we answer in the positive. In connection with this, we invite your attention to Section 391 (a)(14) of the LGC, explicitly provides for the limitation of fines for barangay ordinance at Php 1,000.00, viz: "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Trunkline: (02) 8876-3454

Section 391. Powers, Duties, and Functions. - (a) The sangguniang barangay, as the legislative body of the barangay, shall: (14) Prescribe fines in amounts not exceedinq One thousand pesos (PI.OOO.OO) for violation of baranqay ordinances; Xxxx" (emphasis supplied) From the foregoing, it is clear that the sangguniang barangay shall not prescribe fines higher than Php 1,000.00 for violation of barangay ordinances. In other words, the maximum penalty for barangay ordinances shall not exceed Php 1,000.00. As to the second query, while we answer in the positive, it is important to note and emphasize that an ordinance by the local sanggunian generally enjoys the presumption of validity, which presupposes that the acts of the members Of the sanggunian and the sessions conducted that led to the passage of the measures also enjoys the presumption of regularity and validityl. In line with this, any issues or questions thereon relative to the validity of the subject ordinance should be threshed out in the proper court. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, AU ORITY OF THE SECRETARY: VI OR R. LLAMAS ers cretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs LLNJVRULLLS-LRALLD/1asm copy furnished: MARIA LOISELLA E.
